body.statement: Uniformly over \(P\in\mathcal M\), the explicit local-polynomial learners satisfy \(\mathsf G_n\). In particular, \(\mathfrak B_n=O_P(n^{-2\beta}\log n)\) and therefore \(n^{5/6}(\log n)^{3/2}\mathfrak B_n=O_P\{n^{5/6-2\beta}(\log n)^{5/2}\}=o_P(1)\) because \(\beta>5/12\); bounded foldwise empirical increments give \(\sqrt{\log n}\,\mathfrak R_n=o_P(1)\); and the smooth plug-in estimates give \((\log n)\mathfrak K_n=o_P(1)\) and \(|\widehat{\mathcal V}_n/\mathcal V(P)-1|=o_P(1)\). More generally, whenever \(\mathsf G_n\) holds and \(\inf_{P\in\mathcal M}T_n(P)\ge T_0\), optimized-value stability gives \(\{S_n-S_n^{\circ}\}/a(T_n(P))=o_P(1)\) uniformly over \(P\in\mathcal M\).
body.justification: This separates the actual product, local empirical, variance-normalization, and clock thresholds required at the moving Gumbel level from the stronger instrumental assumptions used to verify them.
body.gap: Published pointwise causal-isotonic LR theory requires a nuisance product small relative to one cube-root neighborhood; the displayed conditions add the logarithmic accuracy needed after scanning order \(n^{1/3}\) dependent neighborhoods.
body.consumer: Three remainder clauses are algebraically supported; the centered V-statistic term and optimized-value stability remain prerequisites for implementation.

obligation.what_is_open: A uniform fold-conditional bound for the fitted validation-fold V-statistic and the implication from the four numerical remainders to optimized constrained-versus-unconstrained LR stability remain unproved.
obligation.obstruction: The within-fold empirical marginalization is a dependent V-statistic, while optimized-value comparison also needs common contact localization and slope envelopes that are not clauses of the transfer condition.
obligation.attempted: The product-bias, variance plug-in, and spatial-volume plug-in orders were proved. A Hoeffding decomposition now also gives the required polynomial scale for the pure bounded marginalization term, but uniformity for the fitted random kernel and optimized-value localization do not follow from that calculation.
obligation.partial_result:
Conditional on the zeroth-order bounds displayed in \(\texttt{lem:learner-rates}\), the definition of \(\mathfrak B_n\) gives
\[
 \mathfrak B_n=O_P(n^{-2\beta}\log n),
\]
and consequently
\[
 n^{5/6}(\log n)^{3/2}\mathfrak B_n
 =O_P\!\left(n^{5/6-2\beta}(\log n)^{5/2}\right)=o_P(1),
 \qquad
 \frac56-2\beta=-\frac16+\frac{d+1}{2s}<0.
\]
Stable product, quotient, and integration inequalities similarly give
\[
 \mathfrak K_n=O_P(n^{-\beta}\sqrt{\log n})
\]
and
\[
 \left|\frac{\widehat{\mathcal V}_n}{\mathcal V(P)}-1\right|
 =O_P\!\left(n^{-\beta_1}\sqrt{\log n}
              +n^{-\beta}\sqrt{\log n}\right).
\]
There is also polynomial slack in the validation-fold marginalization term.  To see its scale, fix one fold of size \(N\asymp n\), a bounded \(C^1\) function \(\phi\), and an interval \(I=(v_0,v_1]\) of length \(h\).  The off-diagonal part of
\[
 \frac1{N^2}\sum_{i,j=1}^N
 \mathbf 1\{A_i\in I\}
 \left[\phi(A_i,W_j)-\int\phi(A_i,w)p(w)\,dw\right]
\]
has a Hoeffding projection in its second argument of magnitude \(O(h)\), a zero projection in its first argument, and a degenerate kernel with second moment \(O(h)\).  Independence of distinct observations and the design-density upper bound therefore give stochastic order
\[
 O_P\!\left(\frac{h}{\sqrt n}+\frac{\sqrt h}{n}\right),
\]
while the diagonal is \(O_P(n^{-1})\).  At \(h=H_n=n^{-1/3}(\log n)^2\), multiplication by \(n^{2/3}\sqrt{\log n}\) still gives \(o_P(1)\).  This establishes the pointwise scale of the pure marginalization term, but a uniform interval inequality with the fitted random kernel and all diagonal and nuisance-residual terms remains to be supplied.  More importantly, the four scalar clauses defining \(\mathsf G_n\) do not themselves state common contact localization or slope envelopes for the two optimized isotonic problems.  A direct integration-by-parts comparison consequently stops at uncontrolled boundary and total-variation terms.
